currentContext.business: IPL manufactures agrochemicals and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) through a diversified portfolio of Technicals, Formulations and APIs, with a product portfolio spanning fungicides, herbicides and other high-value agrochemical solutions. currentContext.expansion: IPL's expansion is built around three Uttar Pradesh sites - Dewa Road (Lucknow, commissioned 1991, 7 acres, fungicides, operating at near-full technical utilisation plus 6,500 MTPA formulations for the domestic market), Sandila (Hardoi, commissioned 2015, 23 acres, herbicides, the largest technical hub at 26,100 MTPA and the base of herbicide technical exports since 2018, with 6 MW of captive solar), and Hamirpur (25 acres, under development through wholly owned subsidiary Shalvis Specialities Limited, insecticides). Hamirpur is the stated growth engine: conceptualised as a ten-block integrated manufacturing complex, with common infrastructure - internal roads, civil works, boilers, utilities and chiller systems - established upfront so that new production blocks can be commissioned with significantly lower incremental capital investment and shorter execution timelines. Two production blocks are operational (Insecticides and Herbicides), two additional blocks are scheduled for commissioning during FY2027, formulations manufacturing commenced there in 2024 and technicals manufacturing commenced in 2026. During FY2026 the Company also commissioned an expansion of its Formulation Division, adding 3,500 MT per annum and taking formulation capacity from 6,500 MT per annum to 10,000 MT per annum, undertaken in view of strong demand (the sentence stating the demand rationale is truncated mid-sentence in the routed Board's Report text). Separately, a new intermediate plant based on indigenous in-house R&D technology was commissioned during the year, part of a backward-integration programme aimed at import substitution of key intermediates and reduced dependence on imports, particularly from China. Management states it is 'well positioned to increase our technical manufacturing capacity to 30,000 MT' from the stated 28,300 MT, and that in-house project engineering lets it commission new blocks and plants in shorter timelines and at lower cost than many peers, keeping capital expenditure efficient. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the narrative chapters; the only rupee capital figure supplied is a Capital Commitments named disclosure, which arrived without a unit line and is therefore not extracted (see capex_disclosed).

risks.note: BRSR material issue #1 (Risk, negative financial implication). The company manufactures pesticides, insecticides, fungicides and APIs, and identifies storage and handling of chemicals such as chlorine and CS2 and flammable materials like fuel as a major process hazard at the site. Mitigation: SOP adherence, scheduled inspections, Quantitative Risk Assessment, HIRA and HAZOP studies and engineering controls as advised by professional safety auditors and international clients' HSE auditors. This is the structural risk of the business model - a single incident is an existential, not incremental, exposure.

risks.risk: Environmental compliance - waste, water and climate/GHG
risks.note: BRSR material issues #2, #3 and #4 (all Risk, negative). Multiple processes generate chemical waste requiring regulated disposal (government-certified agents for landfilling, emission scrubbers, cyclones and dust collectors for boiler micro-waste, PPE management); water is essential to processes and contamination on use/disposal is a compliance exposure, managed through zero-liquid-discharge systems (RO, MEE, Spray Dryer) that are expanded during capacity increases. On climate, the AR states that companies failing to comply with GHG regulations 'may face penalties, reputational damage, and legal liabilities'; mitigation includes an initiated Product Carbon Footprint calculation, renewable energy for Scope 2, biomass for internal steam generation for Scope 1, and employee travel pooling for Scope 3.

BRSR material issue #6 (Risk, negative). Exposure of employees to harmful or toxic chemicals, plus a legal obligation to comply with OHS regulations. Mitigation: mandatory monthly health and safety training for all site employees, quarterly mock drills involving external safety inspectors across shifts, scheduled on-site health check-ups by empanelled doctors, and recurring HAZOP and HIRA assessments with external experts.

risks.risk: Regulatory and legal compliance, including a pending income-tax block assessment
risks.note: BRSR material issue #10 (Risk, negative): penalties, fines or legal action for non-compliance, which the AR notes may extend to 'prohibitions on corporate operations'; mitigated by an expert compliance monitoring system with action notification and internal inspection. Live instance: search operations were carried out by the Income Tax Department in December 2024 at, inter alia, the Company's business premises; a notice requiring a return of undisclosed income for the block period 01 April 2018 to 10 February 2025 was received and filed, a section 142(1) notice was responded to, and assessment proceedings are pending before the Assessing Officer. [provenance for the tax matter: BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 2 (Non-Monetary), routed in the capex_expansion bundle, not in the risks_esg bundle]

BRSR Section A items 21 and 22: 'Manufacturing of Pesticides' is 97% of turnover and the single product line 'Pesticides' (NIC code 2021) is 97% of turnover. The entire earnings base sits in one regulated product category, exposed to the agricultural cycle, monsoon, crop mix, registration/ban decisions and agrochemical pricing - there is no diversifying segment. Not labelled as a risk by the Company.

Exports are stated at 39% of total turnover across 35 countries, exposing the Company to FX, trade-policy, freight and destination-registration risk; management separately flags supply chain disruptions, pricing pressures and geopolitical complexities. On the other side, every manufacturing site is in Uttar Pradesh (Dewa Road/Lucknow, Sandila/Hardoi, Hamirpur) and BRSR item 23 states 2 national plants with international plants Nil - a single-state operating base with no manufacturing redundancy outside it. Not labelled as a risk by the Company.

BRSR item 27: permanent-employee turnover rose to 22.49% in FY 2025-26 from 20.91% in FY 2024-25 and 18.76% in FY 2023-24 - three years of deterioration. BRSR item 25 shows zero permanent workers against 1,443 'other than permanent' workers, i.e. the entire worker base is non-permanent/contractual, alongside 1,126 permanent employees. Gender concentration is extreme (11 female employees of 1,126; 1 woman on a 9-member Board; zero women among 3 KMP). Not labelled as a risk by the Company.

risks.risk: Dependence on imported intermediates and raw-material/supply-chain volatility
risks.note: Management repeatedly frames backward integration as insulation from 'global supply volatility, particularly in relation to imports from China', and the Founder/Promoter Director cites fluctuating raw material prices, supply chain uncertainties and selective geopolitical pressures as FY2026 industry challenges. Until the ten-block Hamirpur build-out and further intermediate plants are commissioned, input security remains a live exposure. [provenance: 'Innovation-Led Backward Integration' R&D spread in the capex_expansion bundle and the Founder/Promoter Director's message in the profile and strategy_outlook bundles; the risks_esg bundle carries only the Corporate Overview version of the import-dependence statement]

one-line thesis: IPL crossed INR 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26 driven by 30% volume growth and successful backward integration in herbicides, with FY27 guidance implying 15-20% growth as new Shalvis blocks and Hamirpur facility ramp up. Margin resilience (18-20%) is secured via in-house intermediate production despite global RM inflation, positioning the company as a key beneficiary of supply chain diversification away from China.

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.

hero.oneLiner: Established in 1984, India Pesticides Limited is an R&D-led manufacturer of off-patent agrochemical Technicals, Formulations and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, supplying leading global agrochemical companies in India and more than 35 international markets from three Uttar Pradesh sites.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Established in 1984, India Pesticides Limited is an R&D-led manufacturer of off-patent agrochemical Technicals, Formulations and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, supplying leading global agrochemical companies in India and more than 35 international markets from three Uttar Pradesh sites.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: IPL manufactures agrochemicals and Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) through a diversified portfolio of Technicals, Formulations and APIs, with a product portfolio spanning fungicides, herbicides and other high-value agrochemical solutions. It supplies multinational agrochemical companies, domestic formulators, traders and exporters, and is progressively backward-integrating into critical intermediates to reduce import dependence. Manufacturing is anchored to three sites at Dewa Road (Lucknow), Sandila (Hardoi) and Hamirpur, each anchored to a distinct product family, supported by DSIR-recognised in-house R&D centres and in-house project-engineering capability.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Strong domestic demand, particularly for herbicides and intermediates
- Exports continued to deliver stable performance
- Improved utilisation across the Dewa Road, Sandila and Hamirpur facilities
- Formulations business demonstrated significant traction, supported by an expanded network of 24 depots and over 350 sales personnel across key agricultural markets in India
- Better realisations in domestic as well as export markets and improved demand across key product segments (Board's Report, 'State of Company's Affairs')
- Expanded formulations capacity and integrated manufacturing capabilities cited as reinforcing domestic and international presence
- EU Technical Equivalence approval expected to improve access to the European market, support export growth and boost export revenues
- Headwinds explicitly flagged by management: supply chain disruptions, pricing pressures, geopolitical complexities, fluctuating raw material prices and selective geopolitical pressures; the Indian agrochemical sector is described as having faced significant headwinds
- Management states it 'remains confident about sustaining growth momentum in the coming years supported by strong manufacturing capabilities, robust research & development infrastructure and expansion in domestic and international markets' - no quantified forward guidance is given anywhere in the routed text
- Strategic investments in plant expansions and a 'substantial capex allocation' are stated to be underway to enhance production capabilities, but no quantum or timeline is disclosed in the narrative

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: IPL's expansion is built around three Uttar Pradesh sites - Dewa Road (Lucknow, commissioned 1991, 7 acres, fungicides, operating at near-full technical utilisation plus 6,500 MTPA formulations for the domestic market), Sandila (Hardoi, commissioned 2015, 23 acres, herbicides, the largest technical hub at 26,100 MTPA and the base of herbicide technical exports since 2018, with 6 MW of captive solar), and Hamirpur (25 acres, under development through wholly owned subsidiary Shalvis Specialities Limited, insecticides). Hamirpur is the stated growth engine: conceptualised as a ten-block integrated manufacturing complex, with common infrastructure - internal roads, civil works, boilers, utilities and chiller systems - established upfront so that new production blocks can be commissioned with significantly lower incremental capital investment and shorter execution timelines. Two production blocks are operational (Insecticides and Herbicides), two additional blocks are scheduled for commissioning during FY2027, formulations manufacturing commenced there in 2024 and technicals manufacturing commenced in 2026. During FY2026 the Company also commissioned an expansion of its Formulation Division, adding 3,500 MT per annum and taking formulation capacity from 6,500 MT per annum to 10,000 MT per annum, undertaken in view of strong demand (the sentence stating the demand rationale is truncated mid-sentence in the routed Board's Report text). Separately, a new intermediate plant based on indigenous in-house R&D technology was commissioned during the year, part of a backward-integration programme aimed at import substitution of key intermediates and reduced dependence on imports, particularly from China. Management states it is 'well positioned to increase our technical manufacturing capacity to 30,000 MT' from the stated 28,300 MT, and that in-house project engineering lets it commission new blocks and plants in shorter timelines and at lower cost than many peers, keeping capital expenditure efficient. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the narrative chapters; the only rupee capital figure supplied is a Capital Commitments named disclosure, which arrived without a unit line and is therefore not extracted (see capex_disclosed).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Backward integration into critical intermediates - indigenous processes developed for intermediates historically imported, stated to reduce import dependence, improve cost efficiencies and reinforce supply-chain resilience; a new intermediate plant on indigenous R&D technology was commissioned in FY2026
- In-house project engineering - the AR claims it 'enables us to commission new blocks and plants in shorter timelines and at lower cost than many of our peers, keeping our capital expenditure efficient as we grow' [provenance: Manufacturing chapter, capex_expansion bundle]
- R&D depth - two DSIR-recognised R&D centres focused on new molecules, intermediates, process improvement and yield; 28 new products (formulations and technicals) registered during FY2026
- Distribution reach - a dedicated sales force of over 350 professionals across 18 states, six zonal offices and 24 depots
- Long-standing relationships with leading global agrochemical companies and multinational customers built over four decades since 1984, with production meeting the stringent quality specifications and HSE audits of multinational clients
- Diversified, resilient production base - each of the three facilities anchored to a distinct product family across herbicides, fungicides and insecticides
- Regulated-market access - EU Technical Equivalence approval for a fungicide product, stated to improve European market access and support export growth
- Pre-built common infrastructure at Hamirpur (roads, civil works, boilers, utilities, chillers) allowing new blocks to be commissioned at significantly lower incremental capital investment and shorter execution timelines [provenance: capex_expansion bundle]
- Sustainability infrastructure as a cost and compliance edge - 6 MW captive solar at Sandila, biomass-based heat and steam, Zero Liquid Discharge, and a product profile in which no technical product falls into the Red Triangle category [provenance: capex_expansion bundle]

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Subsidiary] Shalvis Specialties is a 100% subsidiary incorporated alongside the Hamirpur land acquisition, has its own CEO (Mr. Aditya Kumar Nigam), and now houses formulation production; all headline figures in the deck are labelled "IPL Consolidated" / "Consolidated numbers".
- [Demand] Management flags that "Softer demand for the Company's key herbicide, Pretilachlor, impacted domestic sales during the quarter, while export sales remained stable", alongside "elevated channel inventory" - indicating single-molecule dependence in the domestic book.
- [Board] Mr. Arun Kumar Jain joined as Independent Director w.e.f. 23rd January 2026; Mrs./Dr. Madhu Dikshit is Chairperson and Independent Director.
- [Recognition] CEO Mr. Dheeraj Kumar Jain was conferred the Lifetime Achievement Award by the PMFAI Agribusiness Foundation; the Company also cites the PMFAI Social Responsibility Excellence Award and a CSR Impact Award for its flagship CSR initiatives.
